THE CENTRAL FINDING OF THE ENTIRE INGEST IS NOW ON DISK, on machiavelli and the posthumous audience. Greene Interpretation of the Mastermind case sets out four devices by which Machiavelli built a text to convert resistant readers. First, fill the book with indispensable practical advice on getting and keeping power, which draws in readers of all kinds since all of us think first of our own self interest, and makes even a resisting reader realize that ignoring the ideas might be dangerous. Second, stitch historical anecdotes throughout, since people like to fancy themselves modern Caesars and a mind captivated by a story is relatively undefended and open to suggestion, so that readers barely notice that in reading these stories, or rather in reading Machiavelli cleverly altered versions of them, they are absorbing ideas. Third, quote classical writers while adjusting the quotations to suit your purposes, so that dangerous counsel is easier to accept when it seems to emerge from the mouth of a Livy or a Tacitus. Fourth, use stark unadorned violent language that rouses readers past thought into action and appeals to the young, the most fertile ground from which new princes grow, and leave the writing open ended so readers must fill it in from their own experience and become complicit partners in the text. Greene closing line on the method is that Machiavelli gained power over his readers while disguising the nature of his manipulations, since it is hard to resist what you cannot see. The 33 Strategies of War meets that specification item for item. Practical advice up front. Hundreds of compressed historical anecdotes, which this ingest has documented across five clusters as frequently altered, with dates moved, causes omitted, disputed events resolved toward design, an epidemic left out of a conquest and a coalition that formed reported as a coalition avoided. Margins packed with classical authority quoted without apparatus, including in Strategy 25 an argument of Nietzsche reproduced without naming him. Stark violent register addressed throughout to the ambitious young. And relentlessly open ended transpositions into your daily battles which the reader must complete. Greene describes the method in the third person, credits it to Machiavelli, calls it gaining power over readers while disguising the manipulations, and never once acknowledges it is the specification of the book in the reader hands.
